title: Resolve the runtime flags once per process
why_rejected: p95 regressed 4.18%, above the campaign's 2% rejection threshold.
The change ADDS 370 LOC to a campaign whose purpose is removing them.

The measurement cannot support the claim either way: the cache is gated behind !debug_assertions, and the numbers were taken from a debug test build where the cached path is compiled out. What was measured is the added indirection, not the optimization.
what_was_real: Eliminating 36 std::env::var lookups per token is a genuine defect fix; the mechanism chosen to do it costs more than the defect did.
correct_conclusion: R1's only ACCELERANT candidate does not pay at this implementation. Rust's 1.02% no-product-decision reclaimable surface yields no measured speedup. The Rust tree is dense in both senses: little to remove, and little to gain by removing it.
not_concluded: Whether a cheaper mechanism (compile-time feature resolution, or hoisting the flag read out of the token loop into the session struct) would pay. That was not measured and is not claimed.
